source.section: Instructions PDF p.9, Schedule M line 1d; Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = wages 40,000.00 + Railroad Retirement (person 0) 30,000.00 = 70,000.00. Federal taxable income = 70,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction = 54,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 70,000.00. Schedule M line 1d Railroad Retirement 30,000.00 (exempt in full, no age or income test). Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 30,000.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 30,000.00 = -30,000.00; RI-1040 line 2 = -30,000.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 70,000.00 + (-30,000.00) = 40,000.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 40,000.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 10,900.00 (Single). Line 5 = 40,000.00 - 10,900.00 = 29,100.00. Line 6 exemptions: 1 x 5,100.00 = 5,100.00. Line 7 taxable income = 29,100.00 - 5,100.00 = 24,000.00. Line 8 tax on 24,000.00 by the schedule as numbers: 24,000.00 x 0.0375 = 900.000000 = 900.00. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 900.00. Note: All Railroad Retirement in federal income is exempt: no age or income test.
